subject: Acuity Health — deployment pathways & ballpark pricing
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Smith <kevin.smith@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Maggie Perez <maggie.perez@acuityhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jan 2027 15:32:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: deployment pathways & quick pricing sketch

Hi Kevin / Maggie —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap of what I captured during our discovery and a couple of follow-ups so we can route a pricing recommendation back to procurement: 

Summary of needs (from call):
- Use case: automated clinical note summarization + triage for ambulatory clinics (HIPAA scope).
- Volume expectations: ~1.2M requests/month initially, median payload ~300 tokens in, ~900 tokens out (longer summaries for complex cases).
- Peak concurrency: spikes to ~220 concurrent requests during morning clinic hours.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 450ms where possible for clinician UX.
- Data residency: US-only; must support Business Associate Agreement (BAA).
- Security: preference for VPC/private deployment for PHI; open to hybrid approach for a pilot.

Two deployment pathways we discussed: Hosted API (fastest) vs Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable performance) vs Private VPC/on-prem (full isolation). To make a recommendation I still need two clarifications from your side: 
1) Are you comfortable with a hosting pilot where PHI is redacted at first, with a transition to Private or Dedicated under a BAA for full PHI usage?
2) Can you confirm whether procurement prefers an annual committed infra contract (easier for Dedicated sizing) or a pay-as-you-go approach for the pilot?

Ballpark economics (very rough, for sizing conversation only):
- Hosted API: per-1k tokens model — approximate blended unit $0.0009/token (input+output combined) would put your ~1.2M requests at about $~1.08M/month at current token mix (this includes higher-latency discounts and caching opportunities we can engineer).
- Dedicated (reserved): example 2xA100 reserved cluster (private tenant) with autoscaling burst — estimated starting commitment $90k–$130k/month depending on utilization and model family; unit-cost can drop materially (30–60%) vs hosted at steady state due to GPU amortization.
- Private VPC/on-prem: higher one-time infra & ops cost (hardware + integration) — a rough TCO-first-year delta vs Dedicated: +$0.25–0.6M depending on on-prem hardware choices and support level.

I attached a one-pager with the scenarios and a proposed 8-week pilot scope (pilot_scope.xlsx). Once you confirm the two items above I can turn these into a tighter proposal and a recommended pilot path (my initial leaning: start with a small Dedicated reservation for guaranteed latency + BAA, and send low-PHI traffic to Hosted for gradual migration).

Next steps / asks:
- Kevin: quick yes/no on pilot PHI redaction approach and procurement cadence.
- Maggie: any constraints from platform/security you want us to call out now?

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Smith <kevin.smith@acuityhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Maggie Perez <maggie.perez@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:06:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment pathways & quick pricing sketch

Monica — thanks for the clear notes. A few answers and clarifications below: 

1) PHI approach: for the pilot we need to avoid PHI in Hosted. We'll run a de-identification pre-step for initial tests, then move to BAA-backed Dedicated or VPC for full production. So yes to the staged approach.
2) Procurement: procurement prefers committing annually once we validate the model behavior. For the pilot we need month-to-month billing if possible (or a short PO).
3) Concurrency and latency: 220 concurrency is a realistic peak; the user experience team wants <500ms 95p if feasible. Caching of common prefixes is likely — we can provide a short sample of token distributions after I coordinate with our engineering lead.
4) Security: HIPAA is required; we will expect BAA for any environment that ingests PHI. VPC is preferred for production but Dedicated reserved with private networking will work if it meets our audit controls.

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to sign pilot SOW by end of February and evaluate for Q2 production commit. Procurement contact is procurement@acuityhealth.com — I copied them on this thread.

Kevin
Director, Clinical Platforms
Acuity Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acuity Health — deployment pathways & ballpark pricing

Thanks for the capture, Monica. Two internal notes as we prep the pilot proposal: 

- Given the concurrency/latency targets and HIPAA requirement, a recommended minimal pilot configuration would be: Dedicated reserved pool sized for steady-state throughput ~150–180 rps equivalent (to cover average and allow cloud autoscale for peaks) with a burst pool for morning spikes. That maps to roughly 2xA100-equivalent sustained with 1x burst headroom.
- Pricing approach for procurement: provide three pricing buckets in the SOW — (A) Hosted pilot (month-to-month, per-token) with de-ID, (B) Dedicated pilot (1–3 month reserved at pilot-rate + option to extend to annual commit), (C) Private VPC onboarding estimate (statement of work + infra CAPEX placeholder).

I'll draft a short Rider that shows the transition path and the expected unit economics at 50% and 80% utilization points so procurement can see the break-even vs Hosted. Monica — I can turn numbers into an Excel model if you want; I used the quick math in your one-pager as the seed.

-Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Acuity Health — deployment pathways & ballpark pricing

Kevin / Maggie / team —

Appreciate the quick answers. Attached is an updated one-pager and the pilot scope workbook (pilot_scope.xlsx). High-level recommended pilot path: 

1) Pilot (weeks 0–8): Hosted (de-ID) for feature validation + Dedicated reserved pilot pool sized modestly (2xA100-equivalent) behind a private networking bridge. This lets you validate accuracy/UX on redacted traffic and then exercise PHI flows in Dedicated with a BAA.
2) Procurement model: month-to-month billing for Hosted pilot, 3-month reserved pricing for Dedicated pilot with a conversion credit if you sign an annual commit within 90 days.
3) Pricing examples (illustrative):
   - Hosted pilot (de-ID): $0.0010 per combined 1k tokens — expected pilot run: $18k–$25k over 8 weeks depending on utilization.
   - Dedicated pilot (3-month reserved): $95k/month pilot rate for the reserved pool (covers the 2xA100-equivalent with burst), with an expected blended unit cost ~40% lower vs Hosted at 65% utilization.
   - Private VPC/on-prem: separate SOW; we estimate an additional one-time integration fee $60k–$150k depending on networking & ops requirements.

Requested next steps:
- Kevin: confirm we should proceed with the staged pilot (Hosted de-ID + Dedicated pilot) and procurement preference (month-to-month pilot + 3-month reserved pilot).
- Procurement: if you want a short PO template/quote we can provide a preliminary SOW and a pilot invoice estimate.

If that looks good I’ll file an official proposal in HubSpot and loop Solutions Contracts.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
